title: 5 myths keeping you addicted to OTAs.
styleLine: ONE CONSISTENT LINE ACROSS ALL IMAGES (critical). Cinematic editorial photography, shot as if by the SAME photographer on the SAME 35mm lens, same warm natural grade — deep navy shadows (#262B38) + warm cream light (#F7F8EA), rich but natural (NOT a heavy Instagram filter, NOT washed-out, NOT HDR). Modern boutique-hotel world: walnut wood, cream plaster, greenery, contemporary fixtures. NO dated props. Elegant, quiet, expensive. 4:5 (1080x1350). No text, no logos, no clearly identifiable faces.
note: Path B — scene/organic. Myth-bust, five myths. All six slides are pure photos, no device composites. s1 already delivered. Claims audited: the 65% figure is the campaign-approved ZUZU number and the parity line states what parity actually binds.

slides.headline:
5 ==myths== keeping you
addicted to OTAs.
slides.sub: The stories that quietly decide your channel mix.
slides.imagePrompt: A boutique-hotel owner (three-quarter, face not clearly identifiable) pausing thoughtfully — mid-doubt — at a beautiful modern reception or lounge, warm lamp light, plants, walnut and cream, a small green neon glow. Quietly skeptical, reflective mood. LEAVE THE TOP THIRD a calm darker wall for the headline; subject lower-right. CRITICAL: any darker area must be darker ONLY because the scene's own light falls off naturally — NOT because a dark band, gradient, vignette or overlay has been applied. There must be NO horizontal boundary, step, line or abrupt change of tone anywhere in the frame; brightness must fall away gradually and continuously. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]

slides.title: “They bring guests I'd never reach.”
slides.body: True — and that's fine. 65% of direct bookings still start with a search on an OTA. Reach is what they're good at. The mistake is letting them keep the ==booking== too.

The main subject must sit in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame, leaving a clean, uncluttered, darker LOWER ~40% for text. slides.title: “Guests trust Booking.com more.”
slides.body: They trust a page that loads fast, shows real availability and takes payment without friction. Trust is a ==design problem==, not a platform.

slides.title: “Rate parity means I can't compete.”
slides.body: Parity binds your public __rate__, not your terms. Breakfast, an upgrade, free cancellation to 48 hours, early check-in — all still yours to give.
